planting.note: Direct sow or set out divisions in spring into lean, well-drained soil; keep out of paths and play areas since the spiny burrs cling to socks, fur, and bare feet.

directions: Direct sow or set out divisions in spring into lean, well-drained soil; the ferny bronze-copper foliage spreads quickly into a tight mat that hugs rocky slopes and fills gaps between pavers. It is an effective erosion binder for sunny banks, but the reddish spiny burrs that follow the summer flowers cling readily to socks, fur, and bare feet, so it is best kept out of paths and play areas. Trim back hard in early spring if the mat becomes patchy to encourage fresh, dense regrowth.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into lean, sandy, or rocky soil where richer garden loam would encourage floppy growth.

directions: Plant divisions in spring into lean, sandy, or rocky soil where richer garden loam would encourage floppy growth; this North American native forms a low, glossy trifoliate mat that turns bronze-red in fall and holds slopes against erosion in even the poorest ground. Small white flowers appear over summer above the foliage, and once established it needs little supplemental water. It is exceptionally cold hardy, native to alpine barrens and rocky outcrops from Greenland south through the Appalachians, making it a strong choice for lean, sunny sites where turfgrass fails.

planting.note: Set divisions or plugs a foot or so apart in spring into well-drained soil; tolerates light foot traffic once it has knit together.

directions: Set divisions or plugs a foot or so apart in spring into well-drained soil; the semi-evergreen foliage spreads by short runners to form a low mat that can substitute for turf on sunny slopes or fill spaces between stepping stones. Bright yellow, strawberry-like flowers cover the mat for several weeks in mid-spring, and the planting tolerates light foot traffic once it has knit together. It is drought tolerant once rooted in and needs little care beyond an occasional trim to keep edges tidy.
sources: NC State Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Set out plugs on roughly ten-inch centers in spring; recovers quickly from occasional foot traffic once established, needs virtually no mowing.

directions: Set out plugs on roughly ten-inch centers in spring; this extremely low, tight evergreen mat of glossy round leaves was specifically developed and promoted as a mowable, steppable lawn substitute for hot, dry regions. Deep blue flowers blanket the foliage for several weeks in late spring, and the planting recovers quickly from occasional foot traffic once established. It is remarkably drought and heat tolerant compared with most turf alternatives and needs virtually no mowing, just an annual light trim if it starts to mound.
